title: A second `make ci` in a row fails its coverage check on a host whose live agent scenarios all skip
foundBy: session agent, running `make ci` on two branches in a row while fixing VCR-027 through VCR-029
details:
`make ci` runs the live agent tier near its end, and that tier writes `.coverage/integration`. On a host whose installed agents are not the versions in `test/agents/fixtures.json`, every scenario skips, so that directory holds a run that reached no package.

The next `make ci` starts with `make check`, whose coverage check reads every tier directory it finds. It then fails with `internal/proxy is no longer reached by the integration tier`. Nothing in the tree changed between the two runs.

The message sends the reader to look for a test that stopped running. The cause is a directory left by the run before. Deleting `.coverage` makes the next run pass, and the one after it fails again.

To reproduce, install an agent version other than the pinned one, then run `rm -rf .coverage && make ci && make ci`. The first run exits 0 and the second exits 2.

A tier in which every scenario skipped could be left out of the check, or `make check` could clear the tiers it does not run.
